items.title: Voters reject proposed taxes tied to planned new arena for Dallas Stars
items.summary: Voters in a Dallas suburb have rejected a proposition that would have authorized new taxes related to a planned new arena for the NHL’s Stars.
items.body: PLANO, Texas — Voters in a Dallas suburb have rejected a proposition that would have authorized new taxes related to a planned new arena for the NHL's Stars. Unofficial results from Tuesday's vote in the city of Plano showed 54.6 per cent of the more than 102,000 votes cast were against the single ballot proposal to authorize taxes on tickets, parking, car rentals, hotel rooms and the professional teams that would use the arena. Those taxes were to help the city pay off up to $700 million in bonds it has committed to the proposed $3 billion mixed-use development that would include the new arena. The vote was about the proposed taxes, and not whether the $1-billion arena could be built as part of a large-scale redevelopment project of The Shops at Willow Bend, where the last enclosed mall built in Texas is being demolished. It could include sports, entertainment, retail, dining and public gathering spaces. “The proposed redevelopment at The Shops at Willow Bend remains an important opportunity for our community," Plano Mayor John Muns said in a statement. “We are committed to thoughtful reinvestment and responsible stewardship of taxpayer dollars as we consider what comes next.” The hockey-specific arena would be owned by the city, with the Stars intending to lease it for 30 years. Stars officials hope to move in 2031 about 20 miles north of the downtown American Airlines Center, which they have shared with the NBA’s Dallas Mavericks since it opened in 2001. The leases at the AAC for both teams expire in 2031, and the Mavericks have plans for a similar project of their own away from downtown, about 10 miles north on the former site of a Dallas mall.

items.body: NEWARK, N.J. -- Ryan Nugent-Hopkins felt the significance of his next game and the milestone it represents for the Edmonton Oilers when he saw his teammates Tuesday morning. There they were, all wearing T-shirts that depicted the Oilers forward with a mullet, smoking a cigarette, wearing a short-sleeved camo shirt, and with a tattoo on his arm. On the shirt were the words “1038 games Most Games Played as an Edmonton Oiler.” Nugent-Hopkins hit that mark in a 4-3 shootout loss to the New Jersey Devils at Prudential Center on Tuesday. The 32-year-old forward, selected by Edmonton with the No. 1 pick in the 2011 NHL Draft, passed Kevin Lowe, who played 1,037 games during his 15 seasons with the Oilers. They are the two to have played at least 1,000 games for Edmonton. "I'm very lucky and fortunate to have been able to hit this milestone with this team," Nugent-Hopkins said Tuesday. "It really is a testament to a lot of these guys in this room, and not just the players but the staff, the trainers that have been here for my entire career." After showing him the T-shirts, the Oilers played him a video celebrating his career. "I feel the love," Nugent-Hopkins said. "Having a video that they shared with me was definitely special. To have experienced a lot of these games with a few of the guys in here, it's pretty special. I'm very lucky and fortunate to have been able to hit this milestone with this team." items.title: Jets historic comeback could be the catalyst to save their season
items.summary: The Jets scored five unanswered goals in the final minutes of regulation and OT to beat the Canadiens 5-4.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Winnipeg Jets pulled off one of the greatest regular-season comebacks in NHL history against the Montreal Canadiens Tuesday night, scoring four goals in a two-minute span at the end of the third period to send the game to overtime, where Dylan Samberg sealed it with the OT-winner. The comeback started midway through the third period when Tyrel Bauer took Arber Xhekaj in a fight, followed by captain Adam Lowry dropping the gloves with Florian Xhekaj. The Jets then scored five straight goals on goaltender Jacob Fowler, including two in the final minute by forward Kyle Connor, to complete one of the most shocking results in modern hockey history. On Wednesday’s episode of Daily Faceoff LIVE , Tyler Yaremchuk and former NHL goaltender Carter Hutton discuss Winnipeg’s historic win over the Habs and if it saved their season. Tyler Yaremchuk : I don’t know if it’s just in the moment, but this does something. In that room, this is better than if they just won the game 2-1 and squeaked one out that they didn’t deserve. This has to be galvanizing for that group. Carter Hutton : It’s gotta be. The storyline around Tyrel Bauer and Adam Lowry getting in scraps. You’ve got a younger guy in Bauer taking a fight against Arber Xhekaj. Xhekaj knows he’s a younger guy trying to cut his teeth. All of a sudden, Bauer scores a goal to create momentum. They played great and found a way to come back. I think this is a huge moment for the Winnipeg Jets. At a pivotal point where they just lost nine straight, are they going to stick around after they traded Connor Hellebuyck? Or are they going to weed yourself off into the sunset? items.title: ‘Heavy meat sauce’: Mammoth aiming to stake claim among Central Division juggernauts
items.body: André Tourigny got off the plane with scant knowledge of his new home. It was April 2024, and the Arizona Coyotes were abruptly relocating to Utah. Tourigny recalled watching the 2002 Olympics in Salt Lake City on TV. That's where his personal intel ended. It didn't take long to see what was in store after years of NHL purgatory in the desert. A splashy airport welcome. Plans for world-class facilities. Packed stands — along with thousands more people outside the building — for the players' first introduction at their new home arena. "It's a love story between our players and the fans," he said. "That was amazing." The tough-as-nails Central Division was dominated by the Presidents' Trophy-winning Colorado Avalanche in 2025-26, while Dallas Stars (third) and Minnesota Wild (seventh) were also near the top of the overall standings. Some five weeks into the new campaign, Utah is hanging tough with the big boys. "Heavy meat sauce," Utah defenceman Nate Schmidt said of the Central in his usual colourful manner. "A lot of teams that are really good … there's no real back door into anywhere." The Mammoth sit 10-6-0 through 16 games, good for second in the division, following Tuesday's 3-2 victory in Toronto over the Maple Leafs. items.title: Hellebuyck cites ‘challenging family circumstances’ in letter to Jets fans explaining departure
items.summary: The new Devil netminder had a very unpopular exit from Winnipeg after requesting a trade.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Charles LeClaire-Imagn Images Following a tumultuous exit from Manitoba, former Winnipeg Jets goaltender Connor Hellebuyck is explaining why he wanted out of town. On his personal Instagram, Hellebuyck wrote a letter to Jets fans, giving the reasons why he requested a trade from the only franchise he’d ever known. Hellebuyck stated that asking to be dealt by the Jets wasn’t an easy decision, but he had his reasons. “I know my decision to request a trade was disappointing and frustrating for many people, especially those who supported me throughout my career,” Hellebuyck wrote. “I understand those feelings, and I want everyone to know it was an extremely difficult decision. There were several considerations that went into my decision, including some very challenging circumstances involving my family. After a lot of thought and discussion, we ultimately felt that making a change was the best thing for our family. We’ve chosen to keep those personal circumstances private, and I hope people can respect that.” The 33-year-old’s wishes were finally granted last month, as the Jets sent Hellebuyck to the New Jersey Devils in exchange for forwards Nick Bjugstad, Dawson Mercer and Alexander Command, goaltender Nico Daws, a second-round pick in the 2029 NHL Draft, and a seventh-rounder in 2027. Hellebuyck did add that Winnipeg will always hold a special place in his heart. “I’ll always be grateful for the life my family and I built there and for the people who became such an important part of it. It’s where I grew as a player and where we started our family. … To the great Jets fans who supported me and my family, thank you. I’ll never forget the pride I felt representing Winnipeg, and I wish the Jets and the entire community nothing but the best.”

items.title: Connor Hellebuyck cites family as reason for ‘difficult’ trade request
items.body: In a letter to Winnipeg Jets fans posted on Instagram on Wednesday, the three-time Vezina Trophy winner said "several considerations" went into his move, including "some very challenging circumstances involving my family." "I know my decision to request a trade was disappointing and frustrating for many people, especially those who supported me throughout my career. I understand those feelings, and I want everyone to know it was an extremely difficult decision," Hellebuyck wrote. Hellebuyck, the 33-year-old from Commerce Township, Mich., spent the first 11 seasons of his career with the Jets before asking for a trade last spring after Winnipeg missed the playoffs. The star goalie, who won the Hart Trophy as league MVP in 2025, was eventually granted his wish in October in a deal to the New Jersey Devils . The Jets received prospect Alexander Command, forwards Dawson Mercer and Nick Bjugstad, goalie Nico Daws and two draft picks in return. Hellebuyck, who was moved two days before Winnipeg hosted the Heritage Classic, said in his first press conference with the Devils that he wanted to wait before giving more background on his request. "When I think about my years in Winnipeg, I'll always be grateful for the life my family and I built there and for the people who became such an important part of it. It's where I grew as a player and where we started our family," he wrote. Hellebuyck refused to report to training camp at the beginning of this season, leading to an unpaid suspension and an ugly end to what was mostly a successful tenure with the Jets. items.title: Rangers loan Joonas Korpisalo to AHL for conditioning stint
items.summary: Korpisalo has been on injured reserve since the start of the season due to a lower-body injury.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Credit: Wendell Cruz-Imagn Images A veteran netminder is set to get his wheels under him once again. On Wednesday, the New York Rangers announced that goaltender Joonas Korpisalo has been assigned to their American Hockey League affiliate, the Hartford Wolf Pack, on a conditioning assignment. Per NHL rules, a conditioning stint can last no longer than 14 days. The reason Korpisalo is heading back to the minors is to get in shape after missing a considerable amount of time. The 32-year-old suffered a lower-body injury in the opening days of the 2026-27 season, leading to him being placed on injured reserve. It still isn’t clear when or where Korpisalo suffered the injury. He backed up Igor Shesterkin for the team’s season opener last month. He did appear in one preseason game for the Blueshirts, making 20 saves in a shootout win over the New Jersey Devils. Korpisalo came to Broadway over the summer, as the Boston Bruins traded the Finnish backstop to the Blueshirts for prospect Kalle Vaisanen and a fourth-round pick in the 2028 NHL Draft. Korpisalo had spent the past two seasons with the Bruins, mainly serving as a backup to Jeremy Swayman. In 2025-26, he posted a record of 14-9-6, with a 3.15 goals-against average, a .894 save percentage and one shutout. In 334 regular-season appearances in his NHL career, Korpisalo is 140-126-38, with a 3.06 GAA, a .900 SV% and eight shutouts. He’s in the fourth season of a five-year contract, which he signed with the Ottawa Senators in July 2023. The Wolf Pack are on the road on Wednesday night, facing off against the Washington Capitals ‘ top farm team, the Hershey Bears. Hartford is in the midst of a five-game road trip, which wraps up next Tuesday against the Springfield Falcons.

items.body: Register Login Rangers Assign Joonas Korpisalo On Conditioning Stint By Brennan McClain | at November 4, 2026 9:35 am According to Mollie Walker of the New York Post , the New York Rangers will assign netminder Joonas Korpisalo to the AHL’s Hartford Wolf Pack on a conditioning loan. Korpisalo, 32, has been recovering from a lower-body injury and foot infection suffered at the beginning of the season. The Wolf Pack later confirmed the transaction. Because Korpisalo is on the injured reserve, not the long-term injured reserve, the conditioning loan’s duration is governed by Section 13.8 of the NHL’s Collective Bargaining Agreement, not Section 13.9. Section 13.8 stipulates that a standard conditioning loan may last up to 14 consecutive days while keeping the player on the active NHL roster and payroll. In contrast, Section 13.9 states that the LTIR conditioning loan may last up to six days or three games, whichever comes first (teams may request two additional games). In their last official update on Korpisalo’s recovery, the Rangers announced on October 10th that the 12-year netminder was expected to miss another four weeks. After Walker’s update this morning, Korpisalo is keeping pace with his recovery timeline. His prospective return couldn’t come at a better time for New York. The Rangers were dealt a massive blow in early October when netminder Igor Shesterkin was ruled out for the rest of the 2026-27 campaign with a right knee injury. Before the ailment, Shesterkin had a .927 SV% and 1.79 GAA in five games. Already without Korpisalo at that point, New York turned to untested Dylan Garand to backstop the team. items.title: IIHF maintains opposition to Russia’s reinstatement, silent on Canada’s position
items.body: The International Ice Hockey Federation says it remains opposed to a ruling ordering Russia's reinstatement to international hockey competition, but has stopped short of addressing Canada's refusal to allow Russian players into the country. Prime Minister Mark Carney said Tuesday that Russian players won't be permitted to compete at next month's world junior championship in Edmonton and Red Deer, Alta. The Court of Arbitration for Sport ruled last week Russia must be reinstated to international competition, starting with the world juniors. Russian teams have been banned since Moscow's invasion of Ukraine in 2022. In a statement Wednesday after a council meeting, the IIHF cited significant logistical, security and competitive challenges with Russia's immediate return, including visa requirements and potential changes to tournament formats. "The global impact of the decision made by the CAS Panel and the challenges it creates for all involved were significantly underestimated," the federation said. The IIHF did not directly address Carney's announcement but said it is consulting national hockey associations, tournament organizers and host authorities before determining its next steps. The federation said its priorities remain the safety of players, officials and fans, along with the smooth operation and integrity of its tournaments. It promised more information in the coming days. Carney said Tuesday that Russian and Belarusian athletes will not be allowed to represent their countries in Canada as long as the war in Ukraine continues. items.body: The Hall’s annual Induction Weekend kicks off this Saturday, a celebration of the Class of 2026 ‘s official enshrinement into hockey immortality. But today we’re not interested in who’s already been honored. We want to know which current superstars are future Hall of Famers. Four years ago, my Hall of Fame player ranking tool, the Pidutti Point Share (PPS) system, got its big break on Daily Faceoff . In the years since, early November has become the ideal time to revisit the Hall trajectories of the NHL’s active stars. Which icons have already secured plaques? Which borderline talents should join the legends? Which household names may fall short? How is the standard evolving? We’re going to move fast and check in on 48 active Hall candidates. The league’s top players will be tiered by PPS. The data-driven methodology serves as a starting point for debates. It uses era-neutral inputs to equitably measure a player’s career in a single digit, eliminating reputational biases. How does it work? items.body: VANCOUVER — Asked about the opportunity he is getting with the Vancouver Canucks , Jacob Quillan said: “This is everything.” A scoring star in college, the 24-year-old showed Tuesday night he is willing to do anything to stay in the National Hockey League by delivering the hit of the game and then fighting twice as the Canucks lost 5-4 to the Anaheim Ducks at Rogers Arena. Quillan did fine in his first two NHL fights when challenged by six-foot-five Roger McQueen, then rugged defenceman Travis Mitchell. He can’t build his career on fighting. But his willingness to stand up for himself — to show his new Canuck teammates he will fight for them — was notable on a night when Vancouver couldn’t survive its penalty killing or Ducks sniper Cutter Gauthier, but literally and figuratively battled their way back into the game against one of the league’s biggest teams. It was another game in which the rebuilding Canucks, even with their many flaws, were fully engaged, combative and played their opponents even at five-on-five. Down three goals in the third period, the Canucks surged back with a pair of goals from Jake DeBrusk and generated significant offensive-zone pressure at the end. Jonathan Lekkerimaki just missed on a couple of shot-pass redirects from the high slot as Vancouver attacked six-against-five before losing for the 13 th time in 14 games. For the Canadiens had a 4-0 lead with 2:40 to play, and when Cole Caufield , who scored two of their goals, said it should’ve ended well before they lost in overtime, he was right. This week spotlights a unique New York Rangers broadcaster whose other life happens to be as chief operating officer of a thriving Brooklyn beverage company. There are not enough hours in a 24-hour day for Dave Starman, but somehow he makes do with his dream job and family business. Between his role as radio analyst of the New York Rangers and chief operating officer of the Autotap Corporation, Starman, 58, is busier than a paperhanger with an itch. "I adore every minute of it," Starman said in an email, "and I never get tired because I love both my jobs." Autotap is service provider of fountain beverage services started by Starman's great grandfather, Joseph, in 1900 and incorporated in 1925. "My job is to supervise sales, service and installation of fountain beverage equipment, soda, beer and wine systems," Starman said. "I also keep track of 10 trucks handling delivery routes throughout the city." And without taking a deep breath, Starman personally answers every customer email "because we care about them." items.body: Facebook icon Twitter icon Reddit icon Copy icon Link Copied Add RMNB as a preferred source on Google WASHINGTON, DC — Logan Thompson isn’t used to getting the hook. Capitals head coach Spencer Carbery has rarely pulled the goaltender during his tenure in DC, opting to let the starter hold the net even during lackluster performances. Tuesday night, however, Carbery broke from that pattern, ending Thompson’s night early as Washington fell 6-5 to the Dallas Stars . Thompson allowed one goal on seven first-period shots, but it was Jason Robertson who put the final nail in the coffin, scoring a natural hat trick in the second period before Carbery made his call. Robertson’s first goal came on the power play, the tail end of Tom Wilson ’s first-period roughing minor. After a feed from Wyatt Johnston near the blue line, Robertson shot from the left circle, threading the needle between Thompson’s right pad and his catching glove. Shortly after, a play that began in the Capitals’ offensive zone doubled their deficit. Tyler Myers sent the puck down the ice for Arttu Hyry to carry past the opposite blue line before Robertson regained the puck. Robertson fired from just inside the right faceoff circle, this time sending his shot over Thompson’s shoulder before he could bring up his blocker. For such a speedy hat trick, it’s only fitting that Robertson’s final goal came just six seconds after a faceoff, this time with the furthest shot yet. items.title: Jets pull record latest four-goal comeback in NHL history to end drought
items.summary: The Jets had lost nine straight games prior to the shocking late-game effort.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources If any Winnipeg Jets fans left the Bell Centre early to beat the traffic, you’re in for a rude awakening. The Jets failed to score through 57:21 against the Montreal Canadiens on Tuesday. But after Tyrel Bauer scored his first career goal, everything changed. The Jets ended up scoring three more goals to complete the latest four-goal comeback victory in NHL history. The previous record was set on Nov. 10, 2007, when the Los Angeles Kings scored four goals against Dallas after the 52:46 mark. According to the NHL, this is just the fourth time this has occured after the 50:00 mark, and just the first to have it happen in the final five minutes of a game. Montreal looked in full control, with Owen Beck, Josh Anderson, Cole Caufield (twice) finding the back of the net. Bauer’s goal put an end to Jacob Fowler’s shutout effort, and, seemingly, that felt like the only thing the Jets could get excited about. Instead, Morgan Barron scored less than a minute later, and Kyle Connor made it a one-goal game at 19:00. Just 27 seconds later, Connor recorded his second of the night and 13th of the season, sending the game in overtime after the Jets scored four goals in 2:39 of regulation. Winnipeg wouldn’t stop there. At 3:30 in overtime, Dylan Samberg’s snap shot would beat Fowler to give the Jets the stunning overtime victory, ending the team’s nine-game losing streak in the process. Their last win came on October 13, a 5-2 victory over Minnesota. The Jets finished the game with a 47-22 shot advantage. Notably, this was Montreal’s first game with the club’s new Hometown Remix jersey. The Jets will look to keep the momentum alive on Nov. 5 when the team hosts the Vancouver Canucks.

items.body: Register Login John Gibson Exits Game With Lower-Body Injury By Ryan Long | at November 3, 2026 8:04 pm Red Wings goaltender John Gibson left tonight’s game against the Lightning with a lower-body injury and will not return, the team announced . Gibson allowed two goals on 11 shots while playing the entire first period, and it isn’t exactly clear when he was hurt. If he misses more time, Daniil Tarasov would take over as Detroit’s starter and the Red Wings would need to recall a goaltender from AHL Grand Rapids to fill out the roster. This is the second time in less than two weeks that Gibson has left a game early. He sat out the third period of Detroit’s 5-2 win over the Canucks on October 22 with what the team called an upper-body injury, but he was back in net two days later in Calgary. The 33-year-old has struggled early this season. Gibson came into tonight 4-5-1 with a 3.37 GAA and an .860 save percentage in 10 appearances. That’s a sharp drop from his first season in Detroit, when he went 29-22-4 with a 2.72 GAA and a .901 save percentage in 57 games, his heaviest workload since 2018-19. He is in the final year of his contract, which carries a $6.4MM cap hit. Tarasov has been strong in limited work since signing a one-year, $2MM deal with Detroit in free agency on July 1. In his first start with the club, the 27-year-old stopped all 30 shots he faced in regulation and overtime in a 1-0 shootout loss in Montreal. In Grand Rapids, Michal Postava has opened the AHL season 5-0 with a 1.20 GAA and a .955 save percentage. The undrafted 24-year-old leads all AHL goaltenders in save percentage and is tied for first in wins.

items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Pablo Robles-Imagn Images As if Hockeytown needs even more bad news. As the second period between the Detroit Red Wings and Tampa Bay Lightning began Tuesday night, Red Wings goaltender John Gibson didn’t take the ice. The team later announced that Gibson wouldn’t return to the contest due to a lower-body injury. Gibson gave up two goals on 13 shots in the opening 20 minutes, as the Red Wings found themselves trailing 2-0 heading into the first intermission. Daniil Tarasov entered the game in relief, less than 24 hours after earning the win against his former team, the Florida Panthers . This is far from the first time Gibson has been hurt in his NHL career, and it isn’t the first time he’s had to prematurely leave a game this season. Back on Oct. 22, he suffered an upper-body injury in a game against the Vancouver Canucks , but returned to the crease two nights later. While it’s too early to tell the severity of Gibson’s injury and how long he could be out of action, Detroit doesn’t have a whole lot of time to waste, as the team returns home on Thursday night to host the Vegas Golden Knights. If Gibson’s injury is more than a small tweak, expect Michal Postava to be called up from the Grand Rapids Griffins, the Red Wings’ American Hockey League affiliate. Postava picked up a win in his first NHL start last Monday and was just named the AHL’s goaltender of the month. Gibson has been Detroit’s No. 1 netminder since he came to the Original Six franchise in June 2025. However, he hasn’t nearly had as strong a start to this season as he did last year. In his first 10 starts, the 33-year-old is 4-5-1, with a 3.37 goals-against average and an .860 save percentage.

items.body: Center has four points in 14 games this season; Seattle receives Wood in return Shane Wright was traded to the Nashville Predators by the Seattle Kraken for Matthew Wood on Sunday. Wright, the No. 4 pick in the 2022 NHL Draft, has four points (three goals, one assist) in 14 games this season. The center played 167 games with the Kraken since the start of 2024-25 after playing the majority of the previous season with Coachella Valley of the American Hockey League. "I was surprised, but I was excited as well," Wright said Monday. "Really unbelievable city and organization. I'm excited to be here. "I think, for me, I always wanted a little more opportunity. I wanted to have more minutes. I wanted to play a bigger role, whether that was in Seattle or somewhere else. I was happy to do that, but I'm moving on from the situation and happy to be here. I'm still young, so I want to hopefully be here for a number of years, build something special here and be part of a winning culture and a winning group." The 22-year-old has 82 points (39 goals, 43 assists) in 183 NHL games. Wright had nine points (two goals, seven assists) in 24 AHL playoff games in 2023, helping Coachella Valley reach the Calder Cup Finals before losing to Hershey. "For us, we just felt it made sense for quite a few reasons," Predators general manager Chris MacFarland said. "We're excited to add Shane. We feel he's a natural fit in the middle of the ice. We feel we've got a great opportunity for him to improve day by day. He'll be a better player in the spring than he is now, and he'll be a better player next fall than he is now. items.body: Team will honor late country legend on shoulder of new sweater design during warmups on Nov. 7 If you thought the Nashville Predators Hometown Remix jersey couldn’t get any more “honky-tonk,” think again. On Tuesday, the team unveiled a special Dolly Parton jersey patch that will be worn on sweaters during warmups before the team’s matchup against the St. Louis Blues on Saturday, Nov. 7 (1 p.m. ET; STLNHL, BN+, NHLN, SN+, SCRIPPS). Modeling the new addition to the jerseys was Predators legend Pekka Rinne , who spent his entire 15-year NHL career in Nashville. The patches feature a golden butterfly – one of Parton’s iconic symbols – to honor the “Queen of Country,” who died in August in Nashville. In addition to the patches, the warmup sweaters will have “Dolly” on the nameplates with each players’ number. After warmups, the jerseys will be signed and auctioned off through the Nashville Predators Foundation with proceeds benefiting Dolly Parton’s Imagination Library and the Monroe Carell Jr. Children’s Hospital at Vanderbilt. items.body: CALGARY - For years, Jarome Iginla played through just about everything hockey could throw at him. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: James Guillory-Imagn Images A struggling center looks to be on his way back down to the minors, where a larger role awaits. On Tuesday, the Winnipeg Jets placed forward Brad Lambert on waivers, making him available to the other 31 teams in the NHL. If Lambert clears waivers on Wednesday, he’ll become eligible to be assigned to the Jets’ American Hockey League affiliate, the Manitoba Moose. Lambert has been in the lineup for most of the first month of the 2026-27 season in Winnipeg, but, like the team around him, hasn’t done much. In 11 appearances, he has just one assist, that coming in a 4-3 overtime loss to the Chicago Blackhawks on Oct. 15. He has gone pointless in each of his previous five games, last dressing in the Jets lineup last Thursday, when the team lost a tough battle to the Tampa Bay Lightning , 5-4. The 22-year-old logged less than nine minutes of ice time in the defeat. Lambert has a plus/minus of -5 while averaging 9:10 of ice time per game. There was belief that Lambert could see some considerable playing time with the Jets this season. He posted three goals and six points in 25 contests during the 2025-26 season, the most during a single campaign in his brief NHL tenure. However, the organization appears to believe his talent could be used in the AHL. In 42 games in the NHL, the former first-round pick has three goals and nine points. In 173 regular-season games in the AHL, Lambert has posted 36 goals and 70 assists for 106 points, with one assist in nine Calder Cup Playoff contests. The only player put on waivers on Monday was Toronto Maple Leafs forward Bo Groulx. He cleared and can now be sent down to the Leafs’ top farm team, the Toronto Marlies.

items.title: Weegar loves watching Russia play hockey, but says Europe may see it differently
items.body: MacKenzie Weegar says he enjoys watching Russia play in the top hockey tournaments. But the Canadian defenceman says Russia's return to international competition might be viewed differently by European players. "I know those (Russian) guys want to play in it really badly, but it's obviously a different time, and people have their views on it," Weegar said Tuesday before his Utah Mammoth played the Maple Leafs in Toronto. " But I've always loved seeing Russia in the Olympics and in those best-on-bests." The Court of Arbitration for Sport ruled last week that the International Ice Hockey Federation must reinstate Russian teams, beginning with the world juniors, which start Dec. 26 in Edmonton and Red Deer, Alta. Russia and its ally Belarus had been barred from competition since Russia began its invasion of Ukraine in 2022. The ruling has prompted a backlash from several European hockey federations. Sweden, Finland, Czechia and Latvia have said their national teams will not play Russia in international competition. Norway and Denmark have said they will not play Russia at the 2027 men’s world championship in Germany, while Austria opposes Russia’s return. "It's different for those countries out there, right? You don't really feel the impact out in North America," Weegar said. "They have their opinions on it, and so they should. "Hopefully they can solve those issues and get Russia back into it." In NHL locker rooms, some Swedish and Finnish players were reluctant to weigh in, leaving that to their respective federations. "I'm not gonna comment on that," Montreal Canadiens defenceman Adam Engstrom, who is Swedish, said Tuesday morning ahead of a matchup against the Winnipeg Jets. "That's up to them to comment." items.title: Oilers’ Howard out week-to-week with lower-body injury
items.summary: Howard was hurt when he was on the wrong end of a knee-on-knee hit from the Islanders’ Emil Heineman.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Peter Creveling-Imagn Images A young up-and-comer is going to miss an extended period of time. When speaking to the media on Tuesday, Edmonton Oilers head coach Mike Babcock revealed that forward Isaac Howard is considered week-to-week with a lower-body injury. Babcock noted that Howard is doing better and seems optimistic that he’ll return sooner rather than later. “[Howard] is good,” Babcock said. “He’s going to be out a couple weeks, I think. But it’s nothing. It’s not a big deal.” Howard was hurt during Saturday night’s game between the Oilers and the New York Islanders . Early in the first period, Islanders forward Emil Heineman delivered a knee-on-knee hit to Howard in the neutral zone. Howard needed assistance getting off the ice. He returned to the Edmonton locker room and was later ruled out for the rest of the game, logging just 30 seconds of ice time. Heineman was given a five-minute major penalty for kneeing and a game misconduct. For Howard, who has played in all but two games for the Oilers so far this season, he will miss at least the remainder of the team’s road trip out East, which concludes on Tuesday night against the New Jersey Devils . Edmonton returns home on Thursday, taking on the Anaheim Duck s, beginning a four-game homestand. In just his second season with the Oilers, the 2025 Hobey Baker winner has produced a little bit on the offensive end. In 13 contests, he has scored a goal and three points, just a couple off matching his five-point performance from last season, where he dressed in 29 games. The Oilers (11-2-2) sit atop the Pacific Division, four points ahead of the Vegas Golden Knights .

But fans Ryan and June Hamilton made the trek. They couldn’t miss the opportunity to see their two favorite players, Maddox Schultz and Liam Pue, play for their country at the U-17 World Hockey Challenge. “It’s not every day your favorite team is blessed with superstar talent,” Ryan said. “You’ve just got to soak it all in, no matter where they go.” And superstars they are – already. items.title: Checking in on early returns of Maple Leafs’ go-to goalie Sergei Bobrovsky
items.summary: The Toronto Maple Leafs’ decision to sign Sergei Bobrovsky for three years came with enormous risk. Has it been worth it? Adam Vingan checks in on the early returns.
items.body: The Toronto Maple Leafs ’ decision to sign Sergei Bobrovsky for three years came with enormous risk. General manager John Chayka gambled that a goaltender — albeit one destined for the Hockey Hall of Fame — coming off the worst season of his career at 37 would rebound. At least to start the season, the worst-case scenario has come to pass. Sure, it’s a small sample size, but Bobrovsky has allowed at least three goals in nine of his 10 starts, already leading to questions about whether the Maple Leafs should adjust his workload. “We brought (Bobrovsky) in to be there when the pressure ramps up and we need a rock back there,” Chayka told reporters . Unfortunately, Bobrovsky has yet to harden into that rock. His .809 save percentage on slot shots ranks 39th out of 53 goaltenders who have appeared in at least five games this season. It is an improvement from the .789 he posted last season with the Florida Panthers that ranked 64th among 66 qualified goaltenders (minimum 20 games played). But more is expected from the ninth-highest-paid goaltender in that group. (Across Florida’s consecutive Stanley Cup-winning seasons in 2023-24 and 2024-25, Bobrovsky recorded an .839 slot save percentage.) “I don’t try to overthink, I try to stay just with the moment and try to stop the next shot,” Bobrovsky told reporters . “It is a new team. It’s not only me, lots of new pieces, new system, new guys, so we just build the chemistry, build the belief.” All athletes, even those as finely tuned as Bobrovsky, eventually lose their sharpness. In Bobrovsky’s case, his reflexes appear to have slowed. Opponents have been picking on Bobrovsky’s glove hand, which seems to have lost some of its zip. items.body: Register Login Matthew Poitras Suffered Face Injury By Marcus Antonelli | at November 3, 2026 10:43 am Matthew Poitras is not present at Bruins practice, according to Scott McLaughlin of WEEI . The reasoning behind that regards a hit he sustained in the Bruins’ 3-2 shootout win over the reigning Western Conference Champion Vegas Golden Knights. Poitras, while carrying the puck through the neutral zone, funneled a cross-ice pass as he skated near the benches. Braeden Bowman , who was parallel to the young center, made contact with his head, using his elbow to knock down Poitras at 2:49 of the second period. Poitras was able to will himself off the ice and returned with a full bubble shield, but did not play another shift. Poitras ended his night with 3:13 of ice time. Sean Kuraly skated on the fourth line at Bruins practice. Marco Sturm did not provide a postgame update. Bowman received a five-minute major and a game misconduct. According to Frank Seravalli , Bowman has not received any more discipline. As he described it, Bowman made sure his elbow was close to his body; as a result, this is not viewed as elbowing, per Seravalli. Along with the reverse angle showing Poitras skating into Bowman, his head is not ‘deemed to be the principal point of contact.’ Poitras has been a key player for the Bruins this season. The 22-year-old, who has 7 points in 12 NHL games, has gotten more leeway compared to his past two years under the organization, which saw much more time in the AHL with the Providence Bruins. Playing fourth-line minutes at that scoring clip, Poitras has been a major part of the Bruins’ youth movement. He’s within the top-10 scorers on Boston, and is 10th in the entire NHL in scoring per 60 minutes, with 3.78, just playing under 10 minutes of average ice time.

Boston capitalized on the ensuing power play when forward Morgan Geekie scored to put his team up 2-0. items.summary: A court ruling has permitted Russia to compete in IIHF tournaments, including the upcoming U-18 Women’s Worlds.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources A new wrinkle in the saga following an international court’s controversial decision. After a cabinet meeting on Monday, Czech Prime Minister Andrej Babis announced that the country will not issue visas to Russian players seeking to compete in the upcoming IIHF Under-18 Women’s World Championship, set to take place in Ostrava from Jan. 8-16. Babis cited the ongoing war in Ukraine as a major reason the country wouldn’t allow Russia to play in the event. “It doesn’t make sense to me as long as the war in Ukraine continues,” Babis said in his translated remarks. “It would create the impression that war and killing are normal, which we reject.” The announcement comes after the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) ruled on Friday that the Russian Ice Hockey Federation can immediately participate in International Ice Hockey Federation tournaments, ending a ban instituted after Russia’s invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. Babis added that he believes in the separation of politics and athletics, but the CAS’ decision waives that notion. “I agree that politics should not interfere with sports, but this decision brings politics into it.” In 2023, Czechia instituted a suspension of granting visas to Russian national teams. Interior Minister Lubomír Metnar mentioned that it will not change, regardless of the CAS verdict. “The government regulation from 2023,” Metnar explained. “Which prohibits the granting of visas to Russian national teams, is still in force.” Czechia’s firm stance on keeping Russia out of its country has been part of a massive wave of resistance from the IIHF and many hockey federations. items.body: Hockey Hall of Famer, New Jersey exec thrilled to land goalie in trade with Jets Martin Brodeur believed the New Jersey Devils reached the point where a move for an elite goaltender like Connor Hellebuyck wasn't just warranted. It was necessary. New Jersey's core players are entering or firmly established in the prime of their careers. Brodeur, its executive vice president of hockey operations, said acquiring the 33-year-old goalie reflects the Devils' commitment to take the next step. "It's like the window of winning," Brodeur said in an interview with NHL Network on Tuesday. "Our guys are there. You look at Nico Hischier (27 years old), Jack Hughes (25), Jesper Bratt (28), Timo Meier (30), they're (mostly) all in their late 20s, with Jack a little younger. But I think it was time for us to make a move like that. (General manager) Sunny (Mehta) pulled it off, and it's awesome." Brodeur understands perhaps better than anyone what Hellebuyck provides -- a proven No. 1 goalie who embraces the responsibility that comes with being one of the most important players on the team. Hellebuyck made 17 saves Tuesday for his first victory with New Jersey, a 5-1 win at the Dallas Stars in his first NHL game since April 13, four days after being acquired in a trade with the Winnipeg Jets for forwards Dawson Mercer and Nick Bjugstad , goalie Nico Daws , the rights to unsigned draft choice Alexander Command , the Devils' own second-round pick in the 2029 NHL Draft and their seventh-round selection in the 2027 NHL Draft. items.title: Takeaways: Wolf continues return to form as Flames beat Sharks
items.summary: Devin Cooley’s mid-heater injury gave Dustin Wolf a chance to regain his past form. He made good on the opportunity Monday night in San Jose, writes Eric Francis.
items.body: Minutes after Dustin Wolf came in in relief for his first appearance in two weeks, Ryan Huska was asked if his goaltender’s chief goal was to build confidence. “That’s all it is — get his back up a little bit and just go play. He’s a really good goaltender. He gives us a chance to win every time he’s in the net.” With Devin Cooley’s five-game heater stopped by an injury that is expected to keep him out week-to-week, Wolf is already making good on his chance to return to form. Wolf won his second consecutive start Monday in San Jose, stopping 26 of 27 shots in a 2-1 win at a SAP Center rink he’s intimately familiar with. He’s now 11-2 against the Sharks, which includes going 5-1 in the rink in which his family had season tickets when he was a kid. “I’ve got a lot of memories in this building as a fan, growing up watching the Sharks for a long time,” said the native of nearby Gilroy, Calif., who had his grandmother, cousins and an aunt and uncle in attendance. “I didn’t have the start to the year, on a personal level, that I wanted. (Two weeks off) gave me a chance to kind of reset my mind and work on some parts of my game I wanted to get better at. I feel pretty confident in that now.” Wolf was particularly under siege in the final two minutes of the second period, when a Sharks power play had the Flames pinned in their zone for the entirety of Simon Nemec’s too-many-men penalty. With the Flames up 2-0 in the third, Sam Dickinson beat Wolf through a crowd with eight minutes left, but Wolf held steady despite a late Sharks push. As the game’s first star, it’s safe to say he is rebuilding his confidence. items.body: Calls Nashville star 'the most respectful, humble person you could possibly meet' Ben Vanderklok first began working with Pekka Rinne in 2014, when he was hired to be the Nashville Predators goaltending coach. Rinne already was Nashville's long-established No. 1 goalie. One year apart in age, with Vanderklok approaching his 33rd birthday and Rinne his 32nd, a relationship was formed a dozen years ago that continues today. They worked together as goalie and goalie coach until Rinne's retirement following the 2020-21 season. Now they work together in the Predators' goaltending department, with Vanderklok still the goaltending coach and Rinne the club's European development coach and scout. They have become great friends and rely on each other's friendship and insight almost daily. As such, who better than Vanderklok, who will be on hand for Rinne's induction into the Hockey Hall of Fame on Monday, to give NHL.com readers an inside peek behind the scenes at what "Peks" is really like. Rinne's rise began with a reality check pep talk from Harri Hautamaki, his coach when he was a teenager growing up in Kempele, Finland, about 15 minutes from Oulu. "I played on a tiny little team called Kiekko-Laser; that's where Harri coached me," Rinne said. "I ended up having two really good years with Harri, but we basically played in a second-division Finnish junior program, so it was very local games. We didn't travel a lot." Hautamaki, as Rinne recalled, saw more in the goalie than the goalie saw in himself. Systems are important in hockey, particularly in the NHL. It’s the blueprint of how a team plays. But the reason a team plays the way it does is just as important. It is necessary to have a system and an investment in the players in equal measure. That’s what you see from good teams at any level. If a coach can get his players to play to the best of their ability, the chosen system will work better. If you can get 75 percent of your players at their best, you are going to probably have success. You're going to win. Look, I am a fan of the Milwaukee Brewers and what they just did was incredible in winning the World Series. That's not a high-end team talent-wise, but every player on that team was pretty much playing as well as you can play, right? That's the magic of a good coach. How do you get eight out of every 10 of your players to be at, or near, their best? Focusing on maximizing the individual can be successful. items.title: Pastrnak scores lone shootout goal to give Bruins win over Golden Knights
items.summary: David Pastrnak slipped a shot past Carter Hart to break a shootout stalemate and give the Boston Bruins a 3-2 victory over the Vegas Golden Knights on Monday night.
items.body: BOSTON — David Pastrnak slipped a shot past Carter Hart to break a shootout stalemate and give the Boston Bruins a 3-2 victory over the Vegas Golden Knights on Monday night. Boston’s Jeremy Swayman stopped Vegas’ Trevor Connelly, Jack Eichel and Mitch Marner to set up Pastrnak for the winner in the third round. James Hagens scored his sixth goal of the season, and Morgan Geekie added a power-play goal to help Boston to its sixth consecutive home victory. Elias Lindholm, Nikita Zadorov, Pavel Zacha and Pastrnak had assists for the Bruins, who’ve won two in a row following back-to-back losses. Jeremy Swayman made 21 saves. Connelly tied it 7:23 into the third period when he gathered a loose puck in front of the net and slipped it past Swayman. Noah Hanifin and Marner assisted. Mark Stone also scored for Vegas. The Golden Knights have lost five of their last six since starting the season 8-2. They also continue to struggle killing off power plays, having allowed a power-play goal in seven of their last eight games. The Bruins led 2-0 in the second before Stone knocked in a loose puck for a power-play goal, with assists from Tomas Hertl and Marner, to cut Vegas’ deficit to 2-1.

items.body: Register Login Panthers Reassign Cooper Black By Brennan McClain | at November 2, 2026 8:30 pm Now that Jacob Markström has returned from an upper-body injury, the Florida Panthers no longer need an additional netminder on the roster. Before tonight’s contest against the Detroit Red Wings, the Panthers announced they reassigned goaltender Cooper Black to the AHL’s Charlotte Checkers. Unlike his previous call-up in mid-October, Black made his NHL debut this time. Unfortunately, it wasn’t ideal. Black allowed three goals on 21 shots (.857 SV%) and earned the loss against the Pittsburgh Penguins. That was his only start he made during his recall. He’ll return to a familiar environment in Charlotte. The 6’9″ netminder played in 42 games for the Checkers last year, earning a 25-13-4 record with a .903 SV% and 2.47 GAA. This season, Black has managed a 2-1-0 record in three games with a .919 SV% and 2.67 GAA. Meanwhile, Markström returns from his second injury in the early stages of his return to the Panthers. Before his recent upper-body ailment, which he suffered in practice, Markström exited Florida’s October 12th matchup against the Buffalo Sabres after the first period. Unfortunately, this isn’t a new theme for the Swedish netminder. Markström battled through multiple injuries last season, his last year with the New Jersey Devils. He’s been limited to seven of the Panthers’ 15 contests this season. He stopped 24 of 28 shots (.857 SV%) in the loss against the Red Wings tonight.

items.title: PWHL Detroit’s Britta Curl-Salemme to miss 2026-27 after pregnancy announcement
items.summary: PWHL Detroit will be without an offensive star they signed to a three-year contract in the summer.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: PWHL PWHL Detroit will miss one of their star signings in the inaugural season after forward Britta Curl-Salemme announced her pregnancy and said she would miss the entire 2026-27 PWHL season on Monday. Curl-Salemme posted her announcement on Instagram with her husband, Andrew Salemme, confirming she would miss the entire campaign, marking her first time away from the Minnesota Frost, where she spent her first two professional seasons. Prior to her Instagram announcement, Curl-Salemme was left off the USA roster for the 2026 World Championship in Denmark. Fellow PWHL and USA star Kendall Coyne Schofield was also left off, but had previously announced her pregnancy and that she would miss the entire Minnesota Frost 2026-27 campaign, despite signing a contract extension in the summer. Curl-Salemme finished third in PWHL points through the 2025-26 season, posting 11 goals and 18 assists for 29 points across 30 regular-season games. She also helped push the USA to Milan Cortina 2026 Olympic gold, netting six points in seven games in Italy. As part of the PWHL’s first four-team expansion process, she signed a three-year contract with PWHL Detroit, but will no longer play through the inaugural campaign. To his credit, Mr. Schaefer held it together for more than a minute when it was his turn to give a speech before he began to discuss the dedicated space -- which came to fruition with the help of a $150,000 donation from the Islanders Children’s Foundation -- that is designed for children while their parents undergo cancer treatment. The hockey-themed room is filled with Islanders memorabilia and provides entertainment including both air and bubble hockey, as well as gaming consoles. “My wife would be so pleased,” Todd said, his voice starting to crack. “… The room is exactly what she would want. items.body: Register Login Islanders Sign Ben Hutton To PTO By Brennan McClain | at November 2, 2026 6:30 pm The New York Islanders have suffered a pair of long-term injuries in their defensive corps this season. First, Alexander Romanov is unlikely to return this season after tearing his ACL in early October. Second, the Islanders recently lost Ryan Pulock for potentially a month with an upper-body injury. Instead of sparingly using some younger options to round out the blue line, New York has opted for a veteran addition. According to a team announcement , the Islanders have signed Ben Hutton to a professional tryout agreement. It’s the second PTO Hutton has signed over the last few months. During preseason, he signed a tryout agreement with the Ottawa Senators. Obviously, that never turned into a standard contract for the 2026-27 season. Now, Hutton hopes that the second time is the charm. Although he’s had difficulty finding a new contract, Hutton is coming off a period of stability. Around this time during the 2021-22 campaign, Hutton signed a one-year deal with the Vegas Golden Knights. Even though he primarily served as a depth defender, Hutton turned a one-year, $750K contract into a five-year stint with the Golden Knights. The former fifth-round pick scored 14 goals and 48 points in 196 games with a +22 rating, averaging 15:21 of ice time per game. He had his name engraved on the Stanley Cup after the 2023 Stanley Cup playoffs. He went scoreless in two games for the Golden Knights en route to their first Stanley Cup championship.
